import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Job data
jobs = {
    0: {"processing_time": 47, "due_date": 238, "weight": 3},
    1: {"processing_time": 82, "due_date": 281, "weight": 5},
    2: {"processing_time": 50, "due_date": 213, "weight": 3},
    3: {"processing_time": 32, "due_date": 252, "weight": 5},
    4: {"processing_time": 47, "due_date": 65, "weight": 7},
    5: {"processing_time": 53, "due_date": 194, "weight": 5},
    6: {"processing_time": 81, "due_date": 106, "weight": 7},
    7: {"processing_time": 39, "due_date": 254, "weight": 10},
    8: {"processing_time": 30, "due_date": 262, "weight": 6},
    9: {"processing_time": 65, "due_date": 208, "weight": 3},
}

# Create a new model
model = gp.Model("single_machine_scheduling")
model.Params.OutputFlag = 0  # Suppress output

# Create variables
n = len(jobs)
x = model.addVars(n, n, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")  # x[i,j] = 1 if job i is in position j
C = model.addVars(n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="C")  # Completion time of job i
T = model.addVars(n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="T")  # Tardiness of job i

# Set objective: Minimize the sum of weighted tardiness
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(jobs[i]["weight"] * T[i] for i in range(n)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Add constraints
# Each job is assigned to exactly one position
model.addConstrs((x.sum(i, '*') == 1 for i in range(n)), name="job_assignment")

# Each position is occupied by exactly one job
model.addConstrs((x.sum('*', j) == 1 for j in range(n)), name="position_occupation")

# Calculate completion times
for i in range(n):
    model.addConstr(C[i] == gp.quicksum(jobs[k]["processing_time"] * x[k, j] for k in range(n) for j in range(n) if j <= i), name=f"completion_time_{i}")

# Calculate tardiness
for i in range(n):
    model.addConstr(T[i] >= C[i] - jobs[i]["due_date"], name=f"tardiness_{i}")
    model.addConstr(T[i] >= 0, name=f"non_negative_tardiness_{i}")

# Optimize model
model.optimize()

# Extract the job sequence
sequence = [None] * n
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if x[i, j].X > 0.5:
            sequence[j] = i

# Calculate the objective value
objective_value = model.ObjVal

# Output the result
result = {"sequence": sequence, "objective_value": objective_value}
print(result)
